---
format:
  revealjs:
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          <style>
          .py-editor {
            width: 100%;
            min-height: 240px;
            max-height: 400px;
            resize: vertical;
            font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace;
            font-size: 18px;
            line-height: 1.35;
            border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
            border-radius: var(--radius-md);
            padding: 10px;
            box-sizing: border-box;
            background: #ffffff;
            color: #222222;
          }

          .py-run {
            margin-top: 10px;
            padding: 9px 14px;
            border: 0;
            border-radius: var(--radius-md);
            background: var(--color-teal);
            color: #ffffff;
            font-size: 16px;
            font-weight: 700;
            cursor: pointer;
          }

          .py-run:disabled {
            opacity: 0.6;
            cursor: progress;
          }

          .py-output {
            position: relative;
            margin: 0;
            padding: 44px 18px 16px;
            width: 100%;
            min-height: 330px;
            box-sizing: border-box;
            background: var(--color-code-bg);
            color: #e2e8f0;
            border-radius: var(--radius-md);
            border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
            box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15);
            overflow: auto;
            white-space: pre-wrap;
            overflow-wrap: anywhere;
            font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace;
            font-size: 18px;
            line-height: 1.35;
          }

          .py-output::before {
            content: "pet.py";
            position: absolute;
            top: 0;
            left: -1px;
            right: -1px;
            height: 30px;
            line-height: 30px;
            padding: 0 16px;
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
            border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
            border-radius: calc(var(--radius-md) - 1px) calc(var(--radius-md) - 1px) 0 0;
            font-size: 13px;
            letter-spacing: 0.05em;
            color: #94a3b8;
          }

          .py-output::after {
            content: "▌";
            color: #4ade80;
            animation: py-cursor-blink 1.1s steps(1) infinite;
          }

          @keyframes py-cursor-blink {
            50% { opacity: 0; }
          }
          </style>
          <script type="module">
          import { loadPyodide } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.27.2/full/pyodide.mjs";

          let pyodidePromise = null;

          async function getPyodide() {
            if (!pyodidePromise) {
              pyodidePromise = loadPyodide();
            }
            return pyodidePromise;
          }

          async function runPython(codeId, outputId, button) {
            const codeEl = document.getElementById(codeId);
            const outEl = document.getElementById(outputId);
            if (!codeEl || !outEl) return;

            const originalLabel = button ? button.textContent : "";
            if (button) {
              button.disabled = true;
              button.textContent = "Running...";
            }

            outEl.textContent = "Running...";

            try {
              const pyodide = await getPyodide();
              let output = "";

              pyodide.setStdout({
                batched: (msg) => {
                  output += (output ? "\\n" : "") + msg;
                },
              });

              pyodide.setStderr({
                batched: (msg) => {
                  output += (output ? "\\n" : "") + msg;
                },
              });

              const result = await pyodide.runPythonAsync(codeEl.value);
              if (result !== undefined && result !== null) {
                output += (output ? "\\n" : "") + String(result);
              }

              outEl.textContent = output || "(no output)";
            } catch (err) {
              outEl.textContent = "Error:\\n" + String(err);
            } finally {
              if (button) {
                button.disabled = false;
                button.textContent = originalLabel;
              }
            }
          }

          document.addEventListener("click", (event) => {
            const btn = event.target.closest(".py-run");
            if (!btn) return;
            runPython(btn.dataset.codeId, btn.dataset.outputId, btn);
          });
          </script>
---

## 1.1 Hello, Pet! — print() and Strings {.content}

```{=html}
<div class="top-bar">1. PYTHON BASICS</div>
<div class="screenshot-row">
  <div class="callout-box">
    <p class="concept-insight"><strong>*</strong> <code>print()</code> makes Python say something out loud. Text wrapped in quotes is called a <em>string</em>. Each print gives a new line. These are the first lines of our Tamagotchi program — we keep adding to it on every slide.</p>
    <textarea id="code-print" class="py-editor">print("Hello, little pet!")
print("Beep boop!")
print("I am so happy to see you.")</textarea>
    <button class="py-run" data-code-id="code-print" data-output-id="out-print">Run Code</button>
  </div>
  <div class="main-panel">
    <pre id="out-print" class="py-output">Output will appear here.</pre>
  </div>
</div>
```

## 1.2 Name Your Pet — Variables and f-Strings {.content}

```{=html}
<div class="top-bar">1. PYTHON BASICS</div>
<div class="screenshot-row">
  <div class="callout-box">
    <p class="concept-insight"><strong>*</strong> A <em>variable</em> is a labeled box that stores a value. An <em>f-string</em> (the <code>f"</code> before the quote) drops variable values into a sentence using <code>{ }</code>. New lines are added to the same growing program.</p>
    <textarea id="code-name" class="py-editor">print("Hello, little pet!")
print("Beep boop!")
print("I am so happy to see you.")

name = "Mochi"
age = 1
print(f"Hi, I am {name}!")
print(f"I just hatched, so I am {age} day old.")</textarea>
    <button class="py-run" data-code-id="code-name" data-output-id="out-name">Run Code</button>
  </div>
  <div class="main-panel">
    <pre id="out-name" class="py-output">Output will appear here.</pre>
  </div>
</div>
```

## 1.3 Feed It — Numbers and Arithmetic {.content}

```{=html}
<div class="top-bar">1. PYTHON BASICS</div>
<div class="screenshot-row">
  <div class="callout-box">
    <p class="concept-insight"><strong>*</strong> Numbers do math: <code>+</code> add, <code>-</code> subtract, <code>*</code> multiply, <code>/</code> divide. Feeding your pet is just arithmetic!</p>
    <textarea id="code-feed" class="py-editor">print("Hello, little pet!")
print("Beep boop!")
print("I am so happy to see you.")

name = "Mochi"
age = 1
print(f"Hi, I am {name}!")
print(f"I just hatched, so I am {age} day old.")

berries = 5
apples = 2
total_snacks = berries + apples
print(f"You gave me {total_snacks} snacks.")
print("One apple cut in half is:", apples / 2)</textarea>
    <button class="py-run" data-code-id="code-feed" data-output-id="out-feed">Run Code</button>
  </div>
  <div class="main-panel">
    <pre id="out-feed" class="py-output">Output will appear here.</pre>
  </div>
</div>
```

```{=html}

<div class="screenshot-row">
```

## 1.5 Is It Hungry? — Booleans and Comparisons {.content}

```{=html}
<div class="top-bar">1. PYTHON BASICS</div>
<div class="screenshot-row">
  <div class="callout-box">
    <p class="concept-insight"><strong>*</strong> Comparisons (<code>&gt;</code>, <code>&lt;</code>, <code>&gt;=</code>, <code>==</code>) answer yes/no questions with <code>True</code> or <code>False</code> — called <em>booleans</em>. Careful: <code>==</code> asks "are these equal?", while <code>=</code> just stores a value.</p>
    <textarea id="code-hungry" class="py-editor">print("Hello, little pet!")
print("Beep boop!")
print("I am so happy to see you.")

name = "Mochi"
age = 1
print(f"Hi, I am {name}!")
print(f"I just hatched, so I am {age} day old.")

berries = 5
apples = 2
total_snacks = berries + apples
print(f"You gave me {total_snacks} snacks.")
print("One apple cut in half is:", apples / 2)

stats = {"hunger": 8, "happiness": 6, "energy": 10}
print("Hunger:", stats["hunger"])
print("Happiness:", stats["happiness"])

is_hungry = stats["hunger"] > 5
print("Is Mochi hungry?", is_hungry)
print("Full on energy?", stats["energy"] >= 10)</textarea>
    <button class="py-run" data-code-id="code-hungry" data-output-id="out-hungry">Run Code</button>
  </div>
  <div class="main-panel">
    <pre id="out-hungry" class="py-output">Output will appear here.</pre>
  </div>
</div>
```

## 1.6 Make a Choice — if / elif / else {.content}

```{=html}
<div class="top-bar">1. PYTHON BASICS</div>
<div class="screenshot-row">
  <div class="callout-box">
    <p class="concept-insight"><strong>*</strong> <code>if</code>/<code>elif</code>/<code>else</code> lets the program pick ONE path based on a boolean. The indented line (4 spaces) belongs to that branch. Try changing <code>hunger</code> to see a different path!</p>
    <textarea id="code-choice" class="py-editor">print("Hello, little pet!")
print("Beep boop!")
print("I am so happy to see you.")

name = "Mochi"
age = 1
print(f"Hi, I am {name}!")
print(f"I just hatched, so I am {age} day old.")

berries = 5
apples = 2
total_snacks = berries + apples
print(f"You gave me {total_snacks} snacks.")
print("One apple cut in half is:", apples / 2)

stats = {"hunger": 8, "happiness": 6, "energy": 10}
print("Hunger:", stats["hunger"])
print("Happiness:", stats["happiness"])

is_hungry = stats["hunger"] > 5
print("Is Mochi hungry?", is_hungry)
print("Full on energy?", stats["energy"] >= 10)

if stats["hunger"] > 7:
    print("I am starving! Feed me!")
elif stats["hunger"] > 4:
    print("I could snack soon.")
else:
    print("I am full and happy.")</textarea>
    <button class="py-run" data-code-id="code-choice" data-output-id="out-choice">Run Code</button>
  </div>
  <div class="main-panel">
    <pre id="out-choice" class="py-output">Output will appear here.</pre>
  </div>
</div>
```
